:::: {.columns .faust-layout}

::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- A **C/C++** `struct` represents a named data structure, in which one can **store data** of different types, and define **functions** associated (or not) with that data.
- Stored data can be **declared** with the syntax: `type mydata`. They are called **`struct` members.**
- `struct` functions are declared with the syntax: `type myfunction()`. They are called ***methods***. The type represents **the value they return** after executing their instructions.
:::
- We can **define what a method does** by opening a **curly-braces** `{}` **scope** after its name.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="13-24|14-16|17-21|22-23,1|24,13|" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>

struct Sinewave {
    // Stored data: 32-bits floating-point value:
    float phase;

    // Initialization function declaration:
    void init() {
        phase = 0;
    }

    // Processing function declaration:
    float process() {
        // Increment phase sample-by-sample
        // for a fixed frequency of 440 Hz
        phase += 440.f / 48000.f;
        // When phase reaches its maximum (1.0),
        // start from 0.0 again:
        if (phase >= 1.f) {
            phase -= 1.f;
        }
        // Compute and return the sinewave value:
        float sine = sin(phase * 2.f * M_PI);
        return sine;
    }
};
```

```{.cpp code-line-numbers="28-30" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
        }

};
```

```{.cpp code-line-numbers="30-32|4|34-35|6,9-11|37-38|14-26|38,40-41|2|42|" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

struct Sinewave {
    // Stored data: 32-bits floating-point value:
    float phase;

    // Initialization function declaration:
    void init() {
        phase = 0;
    }

    float process() {
```

## Faust: Anatomy of a C++ audio program {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- The `int main()` function is the ***entrypoint of a program***, it is the first function that is executed. It should **always return an integer value at the end**, either `0` if the program exited successfully, or otherwise an arbitrary **error code**.
- Inside of it, we can create an instance of our *sinewave* `struct`, store it into a **local variable**, call its *methods*, and visualize the result (**print**).
:::
- We can now **repeat** the process as many times as we want by encapsulating the `process()`and `print()` function calls in a `for` **loop**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="37-41" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

struct Sinewave {
    // Stored data: 32-bits floating-point value:
    float phase;

    // Initialization function declaration:
    void init() {
        phase = 0;
    }

    // Processing function declaration:
    float process() {
        // Increment phase sample-by-sample
        // for a fixed frequency of 440 Hz
        phase += 440.f / 48000.f;
        // When phase reaches its maximum (1.0),
        // start from 0.0 again:
        if (phase >= 1.f) {
            phase -= 1.f;
        }
        // Compute and return the sinewave value:
        float sine = sin(phase * 2.f * M_PI);
        return sine;
    }
};

int main() {
    // Create an instance of our custom sinewave type,
    // store it into a local variable:
    Sinewave sine;

    // Call its 'init' function:
    sine.init();

    // Now, the following is going to be repeated 100 times:
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
        float sample = sine.process();
        printf("Sample value: %f\n", sample);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

```{.cpp code-line-numbers="4-22|5|7-9|11-21|24,25-26|29-31|33-39|36|42-56" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>

struct Phasor {

        phase += 440.f / 48000.f;
        // When phase reaches its maximum (1.0),

        if (phase >= 1.f) {
```

- We could also have made a ***separate structure*** for the '*phase*' computation, to make it **reusable** in other components or **waveform oscillators**.
:::
- Additionally, let's make the **frequency** of the oscillator **variable**, instead of fixed to `440`.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="7-9|10-11|10-14,5,8|19|29,34-36|47,52-53" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

struct Phasor {
    float phase;

    // We add another struct member:
    float frequency;

    // Add a float argument to the init function:
    void init(float freq) {
        phase = 0;
        frequency = freq;
    }

    float process() {
        // Increment phase sample-by-sample
        // given the frequency set at initialization:
        phase += frequency / 48000.f;
        // When phase reaches its maximum (1.0),
        // start from 0.0 again:
        if (phase >= 1.f) {
            phase -= 1.f;
        }
        return phase;
    }
};

struct Sinewave {
    // Stored data: 32-bits floating-point value:
    Phasor phasor;

    // Initialization function declaration:
    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
    }

    // Processing function declaration:
    float process() {
        // Compute and return the sinewave value:
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float sine = sin(phase * 2.f * M_PI);
        return sine;
    }
};

int main() {
    // Create an instance of our custom sinewave type,
    // store it into a local variable:
    Sinewave sine;

    // Call its 'init' function:
    sine.init(440.f);

    // Now, the following is going to be repeated 100 times:
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
        float sample = sine.process();
        printf("Sample value: %f\n", sample);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Faust: Anatomy of a C++ audio program {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- We could also have made a ***separate structure*** for the '*phase*' computation, to make it **reusable** in other components or **waveform oscillators**.
- Additionally, let's make the **frequency** of the oscillator **variable**, instead of fixed to `440`.
:::
- Now let's make the same `struct` for *triangle*, *sawtooth*, and *square* waves, and let's also add an **amplitude parameter** to them.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="|" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

struct Phasor {
    float phase;
    float frequency;

    void init(float freq) {
        phase = 0;
        frequency = freq;
    }

    float process() {
        phase += frequency/48000.f;
        if (phase >= 1.f) {
            phase -= 1.f;
        }
        return phase;
    }
};

struct Sinewave {
    Phasor phasor;

    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
    }

    float process() {
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float sine = sin(phase * M_PI * 2.f);
        return sine;
    }
};

struct Square {
    Phasor phasor;

    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
    }

    float process() {
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float square = phase < 0.5f ? -1.f : 1.f;
        return square;
    }
};

struct Sawtooth {
    Phasor phasor;
    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
    }

    float process() {
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float saw = phase * 2.f - 1.f;
        return saw;
    }
};

struct Triangle {
    Phasor phasor;
    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
    }

    float process() {
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float tri;
        if (phase < 0.5) {
            tri = phase;
        } else {
            tri = 1.f - phase;
        }
        tri -= 0.25;
        tri *= 4.0;
        return tri ;
    }
};

int main() {
    Triangle sine;
    sine.init(440.f);

    for (int i = 0; i < 48000; i++) {
        float sample = sine.process();
        int n = sample * 40 + 40;
        for (int s = 0; s < 100; ++s) {
            if (s == n) {
                printf("%f", sample);
            } else {
                printf(" ");
            }
        }
        printf("\n");
    }

    return 0;
}

```

- We could also have made a ***separate structure*** for the '*phase*' computation, to make it **reusable** in other components or **waveform oscillators**.
- Additionally, let's make the **frequency** of the oscillator **variable**, instead of fixed to `440`.
- Now let's make the same `struct` for *triangle*, *sawtooth*, and *square* waves, and let's also add an **amplitude parameter** to them.

- In order to make the computation a bit lighter, we could also store the waveforms in **pre-computed table/arrays**.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.content style="padding-left: 5%; width: 110%;"}
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.arange(16384)
y = np.sin(x/16384 * np.pi * 2);

plt.figure(facecolor="#fdf6e3")
ax = plt.gca()
ax.set_facecolor("#fdf6e3")
plt.grid()
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.xlabel("samples", fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('amplitude', fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```

## Faust: Anatomy of a C++ audio program {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- We could also have made a ***separate structure*** for the '*phase*' computation, to make it **reusable** in other components or **waveform oscillators**.
- Additionally, let's make the **frequency** of the oscillator **variable**, instead of fixed to `440`.
- Now let's make the same `struct` for *triangle*, *sawtooth*, and *square* waves, and let's also add an **amplitude parameter** to them.
:::
- In order to make the computations a bit lighter, we could also store the waveforms in **pre-computed table/arrays**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="22|24,26|28-34|30-35|30|31|32|33|34|37-41|39" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

struct Phasor {
    float phase;
    float frequency;

    void init(float freq) {
        phase = 0;
        frequency = freq;
    }

    float process() {
        phase += frequency/48000.f;
        if (phase >= 1.f) {
            phase -= 1.f;
        }
        return phase;
    }
};

const int TABLE_SIZE = 16384;

struct Sinewave {
    Phasor phasor;
    float table[TABLE_SIZE];

    void init(float freq) {
        phasor.init(freq);
        for (int x = 0; x < TABLE_SIZE; x++) {
             float fx = float(x);
             float phase = fx / TABLE_SIZE;
             float y = sin(phase * M_PI * 2.f);
             table[x] = y;
        }
    }
    float process() {
        float phase = phasor.process();
        float sine = table[int(phase * TABLE_SIZE)];
        return sine;
    }
};

int main() {
    Sinewave sine;
    sine.init(440.f);

    for (int i = 0; i < 48000; i++) {
        float sample = sine.process();
        int n = sample * 40 + 40;
        for (int s = 0; s < 100; ++s) {
            if (s == n) {
                printf("%f", sample);
            } else {
                printf(" ");
            }
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
```
